# Unicode confusables provenance

MD095 uses the direct mappings of the **Unicode 17.0.0 UTS #39**
`confusables.txt` data. The retained sources are unmodified Unicode data:

| File | Upstream | Header date | SHA-256 | Bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `confusables.txt` | [security/confusables.txt](https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/security/confusables.txt) | 2025-07-22 | `091c7f82fc39ef208faf8f94d29c244de99254675e09de163160c810d13ef22a` | 745683 |
| `LICENSE.txt` | [Unicode License v3](https://www.unicode.org/license.txt) | none | `e7a93b009565cfce55919a381437ac4db883e9da2126fa28b91d12732bc53d96` | 1995 |

The generated `internal/confusables/table.go` derives, from `confusables.txt`,
each source code point whose direct target sequence is nonempty and consists
solely of ASCII letters `A-Z` and `a-z`. No closure, recursive or transitive
mapping, accent stripping or other transliteration is applied, and mappings to
digits, punctuation or any other character are left out. Unicode's data
license applies to the retained data and the derived table; its notice is
retained alongside the source.

From the repository root, with Python 3.9+ and gofmt installed:

```sh
python3 -B tools/unicode_confusables.py
python3 -B tools/unicode_confusables.py --check
go test ./internal/confusables -count=1
```

Generation and checking work offline, use these retained sources, verify each
pinned SHA-256 and byte size, and resolve paths from the script. `--check` does
not write files. CI checks exact regenerated bytes, and the Go tests re-derive
the ASCII-letter subset from the retained file and compare it with the
generated table entry by entry. The table runs offline with no runtime update;
changing this Unicode version requires a reviewed data/provenance/table change.
